options.name: Documented environment topology with manual promotion gates
options.summary: The Prod / RTL / Dev-Test topology and its ownership are documented. Promotion passes manual gates. Configuration differences between environments are recorded when noticed rather than continuously detected.
checklist: environment topology and ownership recorded per environment
promotion gates listed with what each gate actually verifies
per-environment data policy stated: synthetic, masked or production-derived
secrets and identity confirmed separate across environments
env-specific exceptions registered
each domain's position checked for whether it was reasoned about all three environments or only Prod

questions.question: For every position in every domain, does it hold in all three environments - and where it does not, is that a decision or an oversight?
What is the configuration drift delta between Prod and RTL right now, measured rather than assumed?
Is RTL representative enough to catch what Prod will hit, and what specifically will it not catch?
Can a Prod credential be used in non-prod, or vice versa?

anchors.metric: Known configuration divergences Prod vs RTL

risks.statement: Divergence recorded only when noticed means the real delta is unknown, so an RTL pass provides no evidence about Prod behaviour.
risks.mitigation: Measure the delta once against a defined baseline even if continuous detection is deferred, and publish the number.

risks.statement: Manual gates are the first thing waived under date pressure, and a waived gate leaves no trace in the architecture.
risks.mitigation: Record every waiver with the authoriser, and report the waiver count at steering.

risks.statement: Production-derived data in an environment with weaker controls is a standing exposure that the environment's own documentation rarely reflects.
risks.mitigation: Establish the actual percentage, then either reduce it or raise the environment's controls to match the data's classification.

lld_notes: Publish the three-column position table: for every domain decision, what applies in Prod, in RTL and in Dev-Test.
hld_notes: The HLD should state which environment the diagram represents; a single-environment diagram in a three-environment estate is an incomplete design.

options.name: Asserted parity with automated drift detection and enforced data policy
options.summary: Environments are built from the same definitions with deliberate differences declared as configuration. Drift is detected automatically and treated as a defect. The per-environment data policy is technically enforced rather than stated.
checklist: environments built from shared definitions with declared per-environment overrides
drift detection running continuously with an owner for the drift queue
every deliberate divergence recorded as a decision with a rationale and an owner
data policy technically enforced per environment, not merely documented
promotion gates automated, verifying stated properties rather than approving by signature
secrets and identity strictly separated across environments with no shared credential
RTL representativeness assessed against what Prod actually exhibits
non-prod monitored where it holds production-derived data

questions.question: Is the drift queue actioned, or does it accumulate until the count is meaningless?
Which divergences are deliberate and which are drift - can the two be distinguished automatically?
Is the non-prod data policy enforced by a control, or by a document people are expected to follow?
In what specific ways is RTL not representative, and does that gap cover a failure mode on the critical path?

anchors.metric: Mean time to close a drift item

risks.statement: Drift detection without a resourced remediation path produces a growing backlog that is worse than no detection, because it documents a known and unmanaged gap.
risks.mitigation: Name the drift owner and agree a time-to-close before enabling detection.

risks.statement: Declared divergences accumulate until parity is asserted in name only, and each individual divergence looked reasonable when it was approved.
risks.mitigation: Review the divergence list at each steering forum and require re-justification, not just re-listing.

risks.statement: Bringing existing environments into parity is remediation work that competes directly with feature delivery for the same teams.
risks.mitigation: Fund parity remediation as a named workstream rather than expecting it to happen alongside delivery.

risks.statement: A genuinely representative RTL approaches Prod cost, and the gap between funded RTL and representative RTL is where the residual risk sits.
risks.mitigation: State what RTL will and will not catch at its funded scale, and have that accepted explicitly.

lld_notes: Publish the three-column position table and the declared-divergence register side by side.
State the enforcement mechanism for the data policy per environment, not the intent.
hld_notes: Parity is a stated property with a measured drift figure; the HLD should carry that figure rather than claiming parity qualitatively.

options.name: Ephemeral environments from a single definition with synthetic data throughout
options.summary: Non-production environments are created on demand from the same definition as Prod and destroyed after use, so drift has no time to accumulate. All non-prod data is synthetic, which removes the production-data-in-non-prod exposure entirely.
checklist: every environment creatable from one definition with only declared parameter differences
environment lifecycle automated including destruction, so nothing persists to drift
synthetic data generation covers referential integrity, volume and edge-case distribution
stateful and third-party dependencies handled - these are what make ephemerality hard
a long-lived RTL retained where sustained performance or soak testing requires it, and its drift managed
identity and secrets issued per environment instance with short lifetimes
cost controls on environment sprawl, with automatic expiry

questions.question: Which stateful or third-party dependencies cannot be recreated on demand, and what happens to them in an ephemeral environment?
Does synthetic data reproduce the volume and edge-case distribution that performance and defect discovery depend on?
Is a long-lived RTL still needed for soak and performance testing, and if so does the parity claim actually cover it?
What stops environment sprawl and its cost, given creation is now frictionless?

anchors.note: Target is zero under this option; anything else contradicts the position.

anchors.metric: Declared divergences Prod vs long-lived RTL

risks.statement: Stateful systems, mainframes and third-party sandboxes cannot be created on demand, so the ephemeral claim covers only part of the estate and the remainder still drifts.
risks.mitigation: Enumerate the non-ephemeral dependencies early and state the parity position for them separately rather than letting the headline claim cover them.

risks.statement: Frictionless creation drives sprawl, and non-prod cost can exceed Prod without anyone owning the total.
risks.mitigation: Set automatic expiry, a concurrency cap, and a named owner for the non-prod cost line.

risks.statement: Synthetic data that does not reproduce production's volume or edge cases makes testing pass while leaving real defects undiscovered.
risks.mitigation: Validate synthetic data against historical defect patterns and production distributions before relying on it.

risks.statement: Where synthetic data is inadequate, teams request a production extract, which reintroduces exactly the exposure this option removes.
risks.mitigation: Treat any production extract as a registered exception with an expiry and a named accepting owner, and fix the synthetic gap that prompted it.

lld_notes: Document the environment definition, its parameters, and the full list of dependencies that cannot be made ephemeral.
Record the synthetic generation rules and the validation performed against production distributions.
hld_notes: Non-prod holds no production data at all under this option - the HLD's data-flow diagram should be able to show that as a hard boundary.
